findings.title: Nothing says how a human is told from an agent at the approve call
quotes: WHEN anyone other than the human tries to approve the `pr` gate THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it
nio can't tell sessions apart, so independence comes from the unit, not from refusing an identity
findings.fix: name what makes an approval the human's (for example an explicit human-only flag or a pending-approval file), and add an AC where an agent approves with auto off.

sources.situation: a building or fresh agent runs the approve command. The system "can't tell sessions apart", yet FR-9 and the decision table rows "building agent" and "fresh agent" must refuse it while "human" is accepted. No mechanism or signal is given for the human. AC-11 covers only "auto flag is on", and no AC covers an agent approving with the flag off. The refusal can be a no-op, or it can be bypassed by an agent that borrows the human's invocation form.

the Decisions say nio cannot tell sessions apart, and the decision table has rows for "building agent" and "fresh agent", which are indistinguishable to the code. AC-11 only covers an agent with the auto flag on and an approved verdict. A test cannot say what makes a caller the human (the `--human` flag? a TTY?). The rows "fresh agent / off" and "building agent" have no AC. A tester could not write a test that fails if the building agent were let through.

findings.reason: FR-9 and the decision table must tell the human from an agent, but the Decisions say "nio can't tell sessions apart". No signal for the human is named, and AC-11 covers only auto on with an approved verdict.
findings.note: Q9: approval only through a human-only command, no unruled finding, verdict not stale; merge records nothing; tables aligned (FR-9, AC-11, AC-21, AC-22, AC-23, AC-12)

findings.title: Push, PR creation and the comment have no failure or replay behaviour
quotes: push the branch and open the pull request, have the gate's fresh driver post one comment
findings.fix: say what happens on each failure (the gate stays blocked and says so loudly), make the open and the comment idempotent, and say which comment is current after later rounds.

sources.situation: the push is rejected, `gh` is missing or unauthenticated, or a pull request already exists for the branch. The comment post times out and is retried, or the driver restarts after the comment was posted. The spec doesn't say whether the effort stays at the gate silently with no pull request, opens a second pull request, or posts two verdict comments. "one comment" also conflicts with fix-check rounds, which each produce a new verdict. The human may then read a missing or stale verdict as "no findings".

FR-16 depends on a remote, a push and `gh`. There is no AC for a failed push, no `gh` or auth, an already-open pull request for the branch, or a comment post that fails. A second run could post a second comment against "one comment". AC-7, AC-8 and AC-9 run a real model at e2e level, and a model is not deterministic. A run that happened to raise nothing, or a spurious extra finding, fails the test with no defect. FR-6 also names "needless complexity" and "cross-epic mismatch" and no AC covers either (AC-9 only tests their absence).

findings.reason: FR-16 and AC-19 describe only the happy path (push, open, one comment). Nothing settles a rejected push, missing `gh`, an existing pull request, or a retried or replayed comment.
findings.note: Q9: reuse open PR; one verdict comment edited each round; failed push/PR/comment stops with message; e2e lens ACs pass 2 of 3 on a fixture (FR-16, AC-24, AC-25, AC-7..9)

findings.title: The verdict isn't tied to a commit, and a merge by an agent has no AC that contains it
quotes: Misuse: the building orchestrator drives the `pr` gate itself, or an agent approves the gate or merges the pull request.
Observable: `gh pr view` shows the open pull request and the comment; the branch is unmerged
findings.fix: put the judged head SHA in the verdict comment and the ledger, treat a later commit as a stale verdict, and say what a merge before the gate closes does.

sources.situation: after `APPROVED` is posted, a commit lands on the branch: a hand fix, a merge resolution, or a push from the orchestrator. The comment now describes a diff that no longer exists, and the human merges on it. FR-3 judges the diff "when the packs are built", and nothing fixes which commit that was. The merge half of the misuse line is covered only by "nio merges no pull request" (SC-2). Nothing rejects or contains an agent running `gh pr merge`, and AC-19 only checks the branch is unmerged at one moment. If the pull request is merged while the gate is open, the state is undefined.

findings.reason: FR-3 says only "when the packs are built". Neither the Verdict comment entity nor AC-19 ties the verdict to a head commit. The UJ-1 misuse line about an agent merging is backed only by SC-2 "nio merges no pull request", so a merge before the gate closes is undefined.
findings.note: Q9: verdict names the head commit judged; stale if HEAD moves (FR-16, AC-19, AC-26)

findings.title: In-flight efforts with open findings on an epic can lose them silently
quotes: its closed gates stay closed, its remaining epics close on the suite alone
findings.fix: say what becomes of open epic findings and open ledgers (carried into the `pr` gate, or blocking the switch), and add an AC.

sources.situation: an in-flight effort has an epic whose gate is mid-round, or at the cap with confirmed blockers, or has open fix tasks, when this lands. "close on the suite alone" lets the epic close and drops those findings. The `pr` gate then judges a fresh diff that may not re-raise them. AC-15 tests only the case where gates are already closed and E-2 is "in progress".

findings.reason: FR-12 and AC-15 cover closed gates and E-2 "in progress". Epics with a mid-round gate, capped open findings or open fix tasks are not addressed, and "close on the suite alone" would drop them.
findings.note: Q9: part-way epic closes on the new rule; an epic already in its old jury finishes it first (FR-12, AC-15, AC-28, Decisions)

findings.title: An epic can close on a missing or vacuous suite
quotes: close the epic only when the whole test suite passes, with no reviewers and no rounds
findings.fix: say that no configured suite, or zero tests run, refuses the epic close, and note that the `pr` gate looks for tampering with tests.

sources.situation: the project has no configured suite, the suite collects zero tests, or the builder skips or deletes failing tests to make it pass. Every epic then closes silently on an empty "pass". Removing the per-epic jury also removes the only per-epic check for weakened tests, and the single `pr` gate sees them only at the end. The Decisions section says evidence is reused "only when it ran the configured suite and passed", but FR-1 doesn't require a configured suite or a non-empty run.

findings.note: Q8: moot; epics no longer close on the whole suite, which runs once at the pr gate

findings.title: Spec removes the per-epic suite-at-end rule of a current decision without a change request
quotes: close the epic only when the whole test suite passes
the closing task's review ran the full suite
findings.fix: add a change request against `D-261106-ltsr` and cite it in the spec's Decisions section, or keep the implement-stage tests at epic close and run the full suite only at the end.

sources.situation: `D-261106-ltsr` (current) says the epic check runs the implement-stage tests and the full suite runs only at the end. FR-1 makes the whole suite the close condition for every epic, and AC-1 requires the full suite in each epic's closing review. An implementer following FR-1 runs the full suite at every epic end, which is the rule the current decision forbids. The spec has no change request against that decision.

D-261106-ltsr (current) says the epic check runs the implement-stage tests and the full suite only at the end. FR-1 makes the full suite the close condition for each epic, so an epic whose tasks are done runs the whole suite before the next epic starts. The pack has no change request against D-261106-ltsr, so the spec goes against a current decision without one.

D-261106-ltsr (current) says the epic check runs the implement-stage tests and the full suite only at the end. A builder following FR-1 runs the full suite at the end of every epic, which the current decision forbids. No change request against D-261106-ltsr is cited, so the requirement goes against a current decision without one.

findings.reason: D-261106-ltsr (status human, memory) says `tests.epic` runs implement-stage tests at epic end and the full suite only when the last epic closes. FR-1 and AC-1 require the full suite at every epic close. The spec's Decisions section doesn't cite or supersede it, though the human's Q1 chose the full suite.
findings.note: Q8: epic closes on its tasks' own tests (D-261106-ltsr); full suite once at the pr gate; failing test at an epic's last task stays implementing (FR-1, FR-2, AC-1, AC-16, state table)

findings.title: Spec replaces the per-epic implementation juries that approved verdicts gated, without a change request
quotes: This spec replaces the per-epic implementation juries with one jury, the `pr` gate
findings.fix: file a change request against the approved implementation-jury verdicts, cite it in the spec, and say which of their gates the spec retires.

sources.situation: `V-261031-ag5f` and `V-261030-67dz` (approved, binding) confirmed the per-epic implementation-jury gates of `2026-10-27-implementation-jury`. The spec deletes those gates for all efforts. The pack gives only the verdict titles, so I infer the conflict from them and have not confirmed it against the verdict text. Under the standing rule the spec must go through a change request first.

findings.reason: V-261030-67dz is a spec-gate verdict on another effort's spec, and V-261031-ag5f approved one epic's gate of that effort. Neither binds a later effort's spec. The replacement is the human's own direction (Summary, #77 and #100, Q1 and Q6), and the spec's non-goals and Decisions state it plainly.

findings.title: Spec does not say what replaces the epic line that an accepted change relies on
quotes: and then go on to the next epic's tasks
findings.fix: state in the spec what marks an epic closed once the per-epic gate is gone, and cite `C-261030-abpr` as changed by it, or add a change request for it.

sources.situation: `C-261030-abpr` (accepted) makes `nio flow done implementation-E-n` write the epic line (T-27) and makes claim refuse the next epic until that line exists (CT-17). With no per-epic gate, nothing in the spec writes that line, so after FR-1 closes E-1 the claim could refuse E-2 forever, or silently skip the check. The spec does not say which happens. The pack gives only the change title, so this is inferred.

findings.reason: C-261030-abpr is a build-order fix against the old effort's spec, about where tasks T-4 and T-27 sit in that plan. The epic line and the claim wait rule are implementation (HOW). AC-1 already says what the spec requires: `nio flow status` names E-2's next task after E-1 closes on the suite.

findings.title: State table has no row for a failing suite on an epic's last task
quotes: Given the last task of an epic is done, when the whole test suite fails, then the epic does not close and the effort does not go on.
last task of a non-last epic done, suite passes (next epic starts)
findings.fix: add a row or column for "last task of a non-last epic done, suite fails" with the target state `implementing`, and mark the event as `ignore` for the other gates.

sources.situation: AC-16 says a failing suite keeps the effort from going on. The state table's columns cover only the passing case, so the state after a failing suite is undefined. An implementer can read the table as allowing the effort to move on with no suite run.

findings.note: Q8: epic closes on its tasks' own tests (D-261106-ltsr); full suite once at the pr gate; failing test at an epic's last task stays implementing (FR-1, FR-2, AC-1, AC-16, state table)

findings.title: Provenance tags on FR-7 and AC-6 do not match the template's allowed tags
quotes: THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the existing jury rules to the `pr` gate
[derived: FR-7, FR-15]
findings.fix: retag FR-7 and AC-6 with one of the template's tags, `[human]` or `[default]`, and keep the derivation as a note.

sources.situation: the template in the spec's header allows only `[human]`, `[research: RF-n]` or `[default]`, and FR-7 is tagged `[agent]`. AC-6 is tagged `[derived: ...]`, which the template does not list either. The Decisions section (line on the agent calls) says those calls "were confirmed as written: the human, Q7", so the human confirmed them but the tag still says `[agent]`. The check reports 0 errors, but a reader cannot tell whether the item is a proposal or a confirmed rule.

findings.reason: spec-consistency: FR-7 is now tagged [human], but AC-6 still reads "[derived: FR-7, FR-15, FR-17]", a tag the template does not list, and the fix asked for AC-6 to be retagged too.
findings.note: minor, skipped at the round cap

findings.title: One verdict comment, but the gate runs several rounds
quotes: holds one comment from the gate's driver whose first word is `APPROVED` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`
round ends with confirmed blocker, below cap (fix tasks in `PR fixes`, next round)
findings.fix: say whether the comment is posted once at the end of the gate or once per round, and whether a later comment replaces or edits the earlier one.

sources.situation: Round 1 ends with a confirmed blocker, so the verdict is `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and the state table row `pr gate` has the verdict posted. Fix tasks are built and round 2 (the fix check) ends `APPROVED`. FR-16 and AC-19 allow one comment, so either the first verdict is never posted, or the second verdict can't be posted, or the PR holds two comments. The spec doesn't say which.

findings.reason: FR-16, AC-19 and the Verdict comment entity say "one comment". FR-7 and the state table have a REQUEST_CHANGES round followed by a fix check, so a later verdict has no stated place. The spec doesn't say whether the comment is posted once at the end or per round.
findings.note: Q9: reuse open PR; one verdict comment edited each round; failed push/PR/comment stops with message; e2e lens ACs pass 2 of 3 on a fixture (FR-16, AC-24, AC-25, AC-7..9)

findings.title: Out-of-flow commits can fall outside every split pack
quotes: each requirement-checking lens one epic's diff per juror
A change committed outside the flow on the effort's branch is always inside the judged diff.
findings.fix: state which pack holds out-of-flow changes, for example an extra pack for non-epic commits, and whether `PR fixes` has its own pack.

sources.situation: The diff is over 1,500 lines and a hand fix or merge resolution touches a file. The requirement lenses get one pack per epic, and the commit belongs to no epic, so no pack holds it. Only the integration lens sees it, and only at "summary level". AC-3 and SC-3 are then false for exactly the large efforts. The same gap applies to a `PR fixes` epic, if it counts as an epic for packing.

an effort over 1,500 lines contains a hand-fix commit (AC-3) or a `PR fixes` epic task, and neither belongs to an epic the packs are split by. A test cannot say which pack holds that diff, so the split may silently drop it and break SC-3. Also, only the over-the-limit case is tested. There is no AC at or just under `jury.split_lines`, and no AC for how "summary level" is told apart from a full pack, so nothing fails if the integration lens gets the whole raw diff.

findings.reason: FR-13 and AC-17 give each requirement lens "one epic's diff". An out-of-flow commit belongs to no epic, so no pack holds it, while AC-3 and SC-3 say it is always judged. The spec doesn't say whether `PR fixes` has its own pack.
findings.note: Q9: commits outside any epic, PR fixes included, get one extra pack (FR-13, AC-17, AC-27)

findings.title: The human's approval is unconditional in one table and conditional in the other
quotes: gate closes when no finding is unruled
approves by merging or recording the gate
findings.fix: put the "no unruled finding" condition in the state table cell, and say how a merge by the human moves the gate to `done`.

sources.situation: In the state table row `pr gate`, "human approves the gate" always gives "→ done". The decision table only closes the gate when no finding is unruled. If the human records approval while a finding is open, the two tables give different outcomes. The summary also lets the human approve "by merging", but no state row or transition handles a merge, and SC-2 needs approval of the gate before `done`. A merge made without recording the gate has no defined outcome.

findings.note: Q9: approval only through a human-only command, no unruled finding, verdict not stale; merge records nothing; tables aligned (FR-9, AC-11, AC-21, AC-22, AC-23, AC-12)

findings.title: Fix tasks re-trigger the transition to the pr gate
quotes: WHEN every task of every epic, fix tasks included, is done THE SYSTEM SHALL move the effort to one `pr` jury gate
→ pr gate | ignore | ignore | → pr gate | → pr gate | → pr gate
findings.fix: add a state, or a note on the `pr gate` row, saying that fix-task completion goes to the fix check, not to a new pull request or a new gate.

sources.situation: The effort is at the `pr gate` and fix tasks are created in `PR fixes`. FR-2 says the effort moves to the pr gate when all tasks are done, and FR-1 says a closing epic goes on to the next epic. The state table has no row for fix tasks being built. `pr gate` is shown as unchanged, while `implementing` is the only row where tasks are built, and its "last task of last epic done" column says "pull request opened". When the last fix task closes, the pull request opened step may run again, or the fix check may be skipped, and the spec doesn't say which. AC-6 expects "the gate's fix check follows".

findings.reason: a cited ID or quote is not in the artefact

findings.title: FR-7 applies jury rules that the grill never confirmed
quotes: THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the existing jury rules to the `pr` gate
the capped batch and fix tasks for confirmed findings. [agent]
findings.fix: have the grill confirm FR-7 explicitly, or cite the intake sentence it traces to, and change the tag from `[agent]` to `[human]` or `[default]`.

The stop rule, the round cap and the automatic round are therefore not confirmed by the human. If the human reads "existing jury rules" as something else, the `pr` gate could be built with a different round or stop rule without anyone having ruled on it.

findings.note: Q9: FR-7 confirmed by the human; retagged [human]

findings.title: FR-11 adds a "system closed" outcome bucket that no answer asked for
quotes: the findings the system closed itself. [human]
findings.fix: confirm the three-way split with the human, or drop "the findings the system closed itself" and fix the tag to match what was actually confirmed.

sources.situation: the intake says only "its outcome goes to the human". No grill answer mentions a bucket for findings the system closed. The `[human]` tag claims the grill confirmed this detail, and it did not. If the human only wanted the verdict and the open findings, the extra bucket is unrequested output that the driver must build and report.

quotes: WHEN anyone other than the human tries to approve the `pr` gate THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it
nio can't tell sessions apart, so independence comes from the unit, not from refusing an identity
findings.fix: say the mechanism in observable terms (for example, "approval without the human-only flag is refused") and add an AC for the auto-off case and the building-agent case, or drop the building-agent row.

sources.situation: the Decisions say nio cannot tell sessions apart, and the decision table has rows for "building agent" and "fresh agent", which are indistinguishable to the code. AC-11 only covers an agent with the auto flag on and an approved verdict. A test cannot say what makes a caller the human (the `--human` flag? a TTY?). findings.reason: same as J-1

findings.title: Fresh-driver independence is checked only by skill text
quotes: the jury and implement skills start a new driver for it with the brief as its only input
findings.fix: split the AC. Keep the checkable part (the `pr` gate is a separate unit in `nio flow next`, and `nio flow brief` alone contains everything the gate needs). Move the "fresh session" part to a judged, non-automated check, or mark it as one.

sources.situation: the Observable is a property of skill prose and agent behaviour, not of any output. `nio flow next` naming the `pr` gate as a unit is checkable, but "a fresh one started from `nio flow brief` alone" is not. If the builder ran the gate in its own session, `nio flow next` would still name the same unit and the test would still pass.

findings.reason: AC-10's Observable includes "the jury and implement skills start a new driver", which is skill behaviour. `nio flow next` would print the same unit if the builder ran the gate itself. FR-8 and the Decisions admit nio can't tell sessions apart.
findings.note: human: NIO can't tell sessions apart; skill text only

findings.title: FR-13 split leaves out-of-flow commits and `PR fixes` with no epic
quotes: each requirement-checking lens gets one pack per epic, holding that epic's diff
findings.fix: say where unattributed commits go (for example, an extra pack), add an AC at 1,500 and 1,501 changed lines, and define "summary level" by something countable (for example, file list plus per-file stats only).

quotes: then the gate closes as the round-cap rules say
no round past the cap starts except the automatic one
findings.fix: state the default `jury.max_rounds`, how many automatic rounds there are, and the outcome per ruling (fixed, accepted, rejected) in the AC itself.

sources.situation: AC-13's expected result is "as the round-cap rules say", which a tester cannot read in this spec, so the test cannot assert an outcome. AC-6 relies on `jury.max_rounds` and "the automatic one", but no default value or round count is given, so a test cannot count rounds. FR-10 has the same "same rulings as any capped gate".

findings.reason: FR-7, FR-10 and the Decisions deliberately defer to the existing jury rules (D-261026-r52z, "same rulings as any capped gate"), and the human confirmed this in Q7. The round-cap values and rulings are defined there, so a tester can read them.

quotes: push the branch and open the pull request, have the gate's fresh driver post one comment
Observable: the lens output lists no integration finding.
findings.fix: add ACs for push failure, existing pull request and rerun (still one comment, or a clear error). Give the lens ACs a fixed fixture and a recorded-output check, or state the pass rate over N runs. Add an AC for a cross-epic mismatch, or cut it from FR-6.

sources.situation: FR-16 depends on a remote, a push and `gh`. There is no AC for a failed push, no `gh` or auth, an already-open pull request for the branch, or a comment post that fails. A second run could post a second comment against "one comment". AC-7, AC-8 and AC-9 run a real model at e2e level, and a model is not deterministic. findings.title: The epic line that the claim rule waits for has no home in the spec
quotes: no `implementation-E-1` ledger or pack exists
the effort goes on to the second epic's tasks
findings.fix: say in the spec what the claim waits for when an epic closes on the suite, or record a change request against the CT-17 rule of C-261030-abpr.

AC-1 says no `implementation-E-1` ledger exists once E-1 closes on the suite alone. The spec does not say whether the epic line is still written, or what the claim waits for instead. findings.title: Epic closes on the suite alone, against current decision D-261106-ltsr
quotes: close the epic only when the whole test suite passes
An epic closes only when the whole suite passes; no reviewers, no rounds
findings.fix: either write a change request against D-261106-ltsr and cite it in FR-1 and the Decisions line, or keep the epic check on the implement-stage tests and move the full suite to the end.

findings.title: In-flight efforts: "next epic" versus "E-2 closes on the suite alone"
quotes: Efforts already implementing switch at their next epic
check E-2 closes on the suite alone
findings.fix: say whether an epic already in progress closes on the suite alone, and make the Decisions line and US-4 match.

sources.situation: an effort has E-1's gate approved and E-2 in progress when this lands. Under the Decisions line, the switch happens at E-2's next epic, so E-2 would still be judged by a jury. Under US-4 and AC-15, E-2 closes on the suite alone. The builder cannot tell which applies to the epic already in progress.

findings.reason: The Decisions line says in-flight efforts "switch at their next epic", while US-4's independent test and AC-15 say E-2, already in progress, closes on the suite alone. FR-12 says "remaining epics". Nothing settles whether the epic already in progress counts as remaining or as the one before the switch.
findings.note: Q9: part-way epic closes on the new rule; an epic already in its old jury finishes it first (FR-12, AC-15, AC-28, Decisions)

findings.title: Accepted epic-line rule (C-261030-abpr) is not carried into the new epic close
quotes: no `implementation-E-1` ledger or pack exists
findings.fix: state what records the suite-only epic close and whether CT-17 still holds, or raise a change request against C-261030-abpr.

sources.situation: C-261030-abpr (accepted) says `nio flow done implementation-E-n` writes the epic line and CT-17 says claim refuses the next epic until that line exists. The spec removes the implementation gates but never says what writes the epic line on a suite-only close, or whether the claim check still applies. If CT-17 stays, the next epic is refused; if it goes, the accepted change is dropped without a change request. The spec does not say which. (Inferred from the pack's memory items, not from code.)

findings.reason: It is the same point as J-8 and J-22. The epic line is HOW, and C-261030-abpr is a build-order change against another effort's plan. AC-1 and FR-1 give the observable: `nio flow status` names the next epic's task. The spec need not say what writes an internal line. The finding itself says it is inferred, not read from the spec or code.

findings.title: Undefined setting `jury.max_runs` next to `jury.max_rounds`
quotes: The `pr` gate's own default `jury.max_runs` is 7
the round cap `jury.max_rounds`
findings.fix: define `jury.max_runs` in one place, state how it differs from `jury.max_rounds`, or use one name.

with no reviewers and no rounds

sources.situation: FR-1 says the epic closes with no reviewers, yet AC-1 and AC-16 check a review on the closing task that runs the suite and names failing tests. A reader cannot tell whether the closing task has a review step or whether "review" just means the suite run.

findings.note: AC-1/AC-16: 'the closing task's review' now reads 'review step (its suite run)', so it is not a juror review
